h: Honest Self Examination Reveals the Nearness of Hashem

p: until the end of the psalm,
while the beginning of the psalm
"He makes me lie down," "He leads me,"
"He guides me," etc., "for His Name's sake."
that as long as things go
His providence, may He be blessed, is forgotten by him,
with regard to Hashem, may He be blessed.
But when there happens to a person
that everything is from His providence, may He be blessed,
and he examines his deeds to correct them.
And that is what is said:
and from then on "I will fear no evil,
for there has become known to him
His providence, may He be blessed, with him
For this is the main thing sought from a person:
And this is the matter of the opening
in the holy Zohar on this parshah
to whom Hashem does not reckon iniquity,
and in whose spirit there is no deceit."
that its beginning is not like its end,
nor its end like its beginning:
for the beginning of the pasuk implies
רַק שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חוֹשְׁבוֹ
only that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not reckon it,
that he has no iniquity at all,
"and in whose spirit there is no deceit."
And it speaks there at length,
אֵימָתַי לֹא יַחְשׁוֹב ה׳ לוֹ עָוֹן
"When does Hashem not reckon iniquity to him?
When there is no deceit in his spirit";
that is, that he does not deceive himself
that it seem in his eyes
that his ways are upright and straight.
For this is the husk of Esav,
"For there was hunted game in his mouth":
that he thinks in his mind
For in truth a person must
how he is lacking in his service,
and magnify his sins in his own eyes;
with Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who said on behalf of Klal Yisrael
among the Men of the Great Assembly,
"My God, I am ashamed and embarrassed
to lift my face to You,
for our iniquities have multiplied," etc.,
"and our guilt has grown great," etc.
And therefore the holy Zohar opened
נָשֹׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ בְּנֵי גֵרְשׁוֹן וְגוֹ׳
"Take a census of the sons of Gershon," etc. (Bamidbar 4:22):
because the whole matter of this parshah
but always to take to heart
and mainly in the three things
that are the root of the whole of the first blemish:
And this is the matter of the beginning of the sidrah,
"Take a census of the sons of Gershon":
as is known, that the tribe of Levi,
by the sin of the generation of the wilderness,
and they are always free for the service of Hashem,
"Hashem is his portion and his heritage,"
"They shall teach Your laws to Yaakov" (Devarim 33:10);
because the world is judged by its majority (Kiddushin 40b),
to rectify the three blemishes mentioned above,
in the aspect of their three families,
of the three blemishes mentioned above.
"They shall send out of the camp
and everyone impure through the dead,"
After this, the mitzvah of teshuvah and rectifications.
And at the end Birkas Kohanim is stated,
as we have said many times;
the three blessings of the Kohanim,
to all the souls of Yisrael,
that they too be aroused in their souls
to rectify the three blemishes mentioned above.
Hashem will not reckon iniquity to us,
because there will be no deceit in our spirit;
and through this we will merit the perfection of the union,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר זֶה (בְּמִדְבַּר ז, א)
"And it was on the day Moshe finished";
and there will be before our eyes
His providence, may He be blessed, always,
